channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: 13-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Kokand hotel; suspect arrested
item.description: A 13-year-old girl was sexually assaulted in a hotel in Kokand, Uzbekistan. A criminal case has been initiated, and the suspect has been detained. Relevant expert examinations have been ordered as part of the investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Leads Largest Foreign Delegation at B20 Summit, U.S. Firms Expand Operations
item.description: Kazakhstan brought the largest foreign delegation to the B20 summit in Washington, where U.S. executives detailed industrial expansion and investment opportunities. Discussions covered sectors like energy, AI, and critical minerals, with officials emphasizing strong political support for the commercial relationship.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Addresses Status of the Kazakh Language
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the Kazakh language is becoming a "soft power." Speaking at the 10th Kurultai of the "Qazaq tili" international society, he emphasized the importance of serving Kazakhstan and strengthening unity amidst global geopolitical tensions. He highlighted that strengthening sovereignty involves citizen well-being, innovation, and respect for law.

item.title: President Tokayev Awards State Honors to Several Citizens
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree awarding state honors to a group of citizens for their significant contributions to the social and economic development of Kazakhstan. Awards include the honorary title "Honored Worker of Kazakhstan," the "El birligi" Order, the "Kurmet" Order, and the "Eren enbegi ushin" medal.

item.title: Large Hizb ut-Tahrir Cell Dismantled in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A significant cell of the Islamist group Hizb ut-Tahrir has been dismantled in Kyrgyzstan. Authorities have taken action against the organization, though specific details regarding the operation or the number of individuals apprehended were not immediately disclosed. This action is part of ongoing efforts to maintain national security.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Major Fraud Case at Gold Mine
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's East Kazakhstan region are investigating a large-scale fraud case linked to the 'Manka' gold deposit. The General Prosecutor's Office initiated a criminal case based on a complaint from Z MetalsHolding Limited founders. The investigation is proceeding under the article for large-scale fraud, with the Prosecutor's Office monitoring its progress.

item.title: Issyk-Kul Region Explores New Tourism Avenues Beyond Beach Holidays
item.description: The Issyk-Kul region offers diverse tourism potential, including mountain routes, health resorts, historical sites, and nomadic culture, beyond traditional beach holidays. The State Agency for Tourism Development highlights opportunities in beach, ecological, mountain, ethnographic, health, and active tourism. Archaeological heritage is also a focus for development.

item.title: Aktau Residents Left Without Power After Storm Damages High-Voltage Line
item.description: Five residential buildings in Aktau lost electricity, heating, and hot water due to a high-voltage line break during heavy rainfall. The Energy Minister explained that flooding initially hindered repair efforts. Investigations are underway to determine responsibility for the damaged section of the electrical grid.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizen Recovers Nearly One Million Rubles in Unpaid Wages in Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Development representation in Russia assisted a citizen in recovering 988,100 rubles in owed wages from a Russian company. Since November 2022, the representation has helped 1,643 Kyrgyz citizens recover over 121 million rubles in wage arrears.

item.title: Jalal-Abad Region Considers Acquiring Agricultural Machinery from Belarus
item.description: The head of Jalal-Abad region, Tilek Tekebaev, visited the "Lidselmash" enterprise in Grodno region, Belarus, which produces modern agricultural equipment. Discussions were held on delivering this machinery to Jalal-Abad, its use by local farmers, and developing cooperation. Tekebaev expressed interest in collaborating with the enterprise to enhance agricultural efficiency.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Dollar Exchange Rate Expected to Stay Below 500 Tenge in a Year
item.description: Financial market experts predict the dollar exchange rate in Kazakhstan. By early December, the dollar is expected to be around 462.4 tenge. For the next year, expectations have improved to 499.4 tenge per dollar. Factors supporting the tenge include a widening trade surplus and increased transfers from the National Fund.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Emergency Alert System Delays Explained by Ministry of Emergency Situations
item.description: The Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) in Kazakhstan acknowledges delays in emergency SMS alerts, attributing them to the process of receiving information from "Kazhydromet" and subsequent distribution by mobile operators. The MES is working with operators to expedite message delivery. The Mass Alert system is operational in seismically active regions for faster notifications.

item.title: Videographer Admits Aiding in Granite Tile Theft, Denies Pressure
item.description: Ulan Nusipkozha, videographer for activist Sanjar Bokayev, admitted to aiding in the theft of granite tiles in Almaty but denied being an organizer or perpetrator. He testified that Bokayev instructed him to film the removal of tiles from a construction site. Nusipkozha claimed he suspected theft and that Bokayev later ordered the tiles returned.

item.title: Kazakhstan Road Authority Explains Contractor Won Tender Using False Documents
item.description: Kazakhstan's road authority, KazAvtoZhol, addressed procurement violations found by the General Transport Prosecutor's Office. A contractor won a 2.4 billion tenge tender for Astana-Kabanbai road repairs using documents belonging to a non-employee. The authority stated it cannot verify document legitimacy, placing responsibility on the contractor.

item.title: Jalal-Abad Delegation Explores Dairy Production Cooperation with Belarus
item.description: A delegation from Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region visited Belarus's Grodno region to learn about industrial enterprises. The visit, part of a regional forum, focused on expanding trade, economic ties, and cooperation in industry and agriculture. The delegation toured a dairy plant, expressing interest in adopting modern technologies for dairy production.

item.title: Putin Urges Strengthening of CSTO Amid Rising International Tensions
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin called for CSTO member states to enhance their capabilities amidst growing international tensions. Speaking at a security forum in Moscow, he emphasized the importance of coordinating efforts against terrorism, extremism, cybercrime, drug trafficking, and illegal migration. Putin expressed hope for a constructive forum outcome.

item.title: Illegal Coal Mining in Uzbekistan Causes Thousands of Trees to Be Destroyed, Exceeding 480 Million Soums in Damages
item.description: Illegal coal mining in Uzbekistan has resulted in the destruction of thousands of trees and shrubs, with environmental damages exceeding 480 million soums. A private enterprise, "MEGA AZIYA COAL AND QUARTZ" LLC, illegally extracted and attempted to sell 500 tons of coal. Criminal charges have been filed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Emergency Ministry Admits Delays in SMS Alert System
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations has acknowledged issues with delayed SMS alerts for emergencies. The ministry is working with mobile operators to expedite the delivery of these crucial warnings. While SMS alerts are free, the ministry also utilizes the Mass Alert system for earthquake warnings in certain regions and plans to expand its seismic monitoring network.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 13-Year-Old Victim of Sexual Assault in Kokand, Suspect Detained
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Kokand, Uzbekistan, following the sexual assault of a 13-year-old girl in a hotel. The suspect has been detained and is in custody. The victim is receiving comprehensive assistance, including legal and psychological support. The incident is under investigation, with necessary examinations appointed.

item.title: Bishkek Considers Monorail Project Along Alarcha and Alamedin Rivers
item.description: Bishkek is exploring the possibility of constructing an elevated monorail system along the Alarcha and Alamedin riverbeds. City officials discussed technical feasibility, operational aspects considering Bishkek's climate, and financing options with representatives from Chinese company BYD. A joint site survey and working group formation are planned.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Poland Agree to Expand Rail Freight and Container Train Services
item.description: Uzbekistan and Poland have agreed to expand railway freight transport and establish regular container train services. A memorandum was signed between Uzbekistan Railways and Polish State Railways (PKP). Discussions included attracting new cargo and competitive tariffs. The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project is seen as a future route for Asian goods.

item.title: Tokayev: Adversaries Distort 'Law and Order' Principle, Calling It Unclean
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that rudeness, insults, littering, and vandalism are unacceptable in a civilized society and should be punished by law. He emphasized that the 'Law and Order' principle must be an integral part of public life. Tokayev criticized adversaries for distorting this principle, presenting it as a tool of pressure, which he deems 'unclean'.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Cafes in Residential Buildings Can Be Closed for Fire Safety Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister for Emergency Situations, Murat Mukhanov, stated that cafes and restaurants on the ground floors of residential buildings are subject to fire safety checks. If violations are found, residents can report them to emergency departments. Repeated or unaddressed violations can lead to temporary closure through court orders.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prosecutor General's Office Found Around 15 Business Inspections with Violations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Prosecutor General's Office identified approximately 15 business inspections conducted with violations over the past two years. These included inspections of non-existent, liquidated companies, and cases with missed deadlines or unsubmitted reports. The Prosecutor's Office proposes a new oversight mechanism requiring preliminary authorization for inspections.

item.title: Russian Security Chief Urges Cooperation with Kabul, Warns of Drug Trafficking Threats
item.description: Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu emphasized the need for cooperation with Kabul, stating that developments in Central Asia impact Afghanistan's stability. He warned of emerging synthetic drug trafficking threats, noting the use of contactless delivery and cryptocurrencies. Shoigu called for joint regional efforts to counter these new drug trafficking methods and enhance security cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prosecutor General's Office Transfers Fraud Case to Regional Police
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office has transferred materials related to an alleged fraud case at the 'Manka' deposit to the East Kazakhstan regional police department. The investigation, initiated on June 15, 2026, is being conducted under Article 190, Part 4, Clause 2 of the Criminal Code, concerning fraud in particularly large amounts. The prosecution is monitoring the case.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Escrow System Bill Submitted to Senate for Approval
item.description: A bill introducing an escrow system for shared construction in Uzbekistan has been sent to the Senate. The legislation mandates that funds invested in shared construction be held in escrow accounts at banks, with contracts requiring notarization and state registration. It also strengthens requirements for developers and outlines mechanisms to protect equity holders if construction deadlines are missed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Minister of Energy Pledges to Maintain Current Electricity Tariffs
item.description: The Minister of Energy of the Republic of Kazakhstan has stated that the current electricity tariffs will be maintained. This announcement comes as the ministry aims to ensure stability for consumers while managing the energy sector's needs. Further details on the sustainability of this commitment were not provided.

item.title: Almaty Consumers League Demands Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Water Quality Tests
item.description: Consumer advocates in Almaty are demanding that Pseudomonas aeruginosa be included in water quality testing. The National Consumers League president, Svetlana Romanovskaya, stated that the bacteria was found in tap and filtered water by an independent lab. However, "Almaty Su" claims their tests found no such bacteria.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Over 320 Entrepreneurs Complain About Unlawful Inspections
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Kyrgyzstan received 325 complaints from entrepreneurs regarding baseless inspections. The Deputy Prosecutor General stated that 89% of these complaints were satisfied, leading to prosecutorial protocols. A new bill requires prosecutor approval for business inspections.

item.title: Trilateral Talks Between Russia, US, and Ukraine Begin in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Trilateral talks involving representatives from Russia, the United States, and Ukraine have commenced in Abu Dhabi, focusing on security guarantees. The closed-door meeting, planned for two days, includes delegations led by Vladimir Medinsky for Russia. The UAE is hosting the consultations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Restore 141,000 Hectares of Land with €103.7 Million Investment Under CLiCA Program
item.description: Under the regional CLiCA program, Uzbekistan will restore 141,000 hectares of land with an investment of €103.7 million. The initiative, supported by the Green Climate Fund and other international partners, will focus on reforestation and pastureland restoration in four provinces. It aims to enhance climate resilience for 342,000 residents.

item.title: Former Security Chief Criticizes Emergency Minister's Handling of Rescue Operation
item.description: Former head of the State Committee for National Security, Kamchybek Tashiev, criticized the Emergency Situations Minister's response to the rescue operation for a 14-year-old boy who died on "Elektro" peak. Tashiev stated the minister should have personally supervised the operation from the start and acted without waiting for orders from above.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Dozens of offenses including weapons and drugs found in Namangan
item.description: During a security campaign in Uzbekistan's Namangan region, law enforcement identified dozens of offenses. The operation led to the discovery of illegal weapons, drugs, and unregistered religious teaching. 18 individuals face criminal charges, while 50 others will be held accountable for administrative violations. The crackdown also helped solve 27 previously unsolved crimes.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP urges Prosecutor General to probe minister's orders
item.description: Kyrgyz Member of Parliament Dastan Bekeshev has called on the Prosecutor General's Office to investigate the legality of orders issued by the Minister of Construction, Architecture, and Housing and Communal Services. Bekeshev cited orders restricting pavilion permits and banning electric vehicle charging stations as detrimental to small businesses and potentially contradicting legislation.

item.title: Ten people with HIV sought in West Kazakhstan region
item.description: Authorities in West Kazakhstan are searching for ten individuals diagnosed with HIV. The regional health department reported 44 new HIV cases in the first nine months of 2026, a decrease from the previous year. Currently, 755 people are under dispensary supervision, with three HIV-related deaths recorded this year. The risk of mother-to-child transmission has been reduced to 2%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mandates Employers to Review Salaries Based on Inflation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov signed amendments to the Labor Code, obligating employers to index salaries considering consumer price growth. The law aims to protect workers' purchasing power. The specific percentage increase is not fixed by law.

item.title: Large Opium Shipment from Afghanistan Seized in Uzbekistan's Surkhandarya Region
item.description: Law enforcement in Uzbekistan's Surkhandarya region intercepted a major drug trafficking channel, arresting two men attempting to sell over five kilograms of opium. The drugs were reportedly sourced from neighboring Afghanistan. An investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyz Opposition Figures Demand Parliamentary Investigation into Their Cases
item.description: Opposition leader Temirlan Sultanbekov and Kadirbek Atambayev, son of a former president, have appealed to the speaker of Kyrgyzstan's parliament. They request a parliamentary commission to investigate the legality of their criminal prosecution and closed-door trials. They note international concern but a lack of public statements from Kyrgyz lawmakers.

item.title: Kazakhstan Videographer Admits Aiding in Granite Tile Theft
item.description: During a court hearing, Ulan Nusipkozha, videographer for civil activist Sanzhar Bokaev, confessed to aiding in the theft of granite tiles from a riverbank reconstruction project. Nusipkozha stated Bokaev sent him video footage and encouraged him to film such activities independently, which he initially opposed.
